items.title: Assessment of eligibility for evidence-based pharmacological therapies in acute heart failure across heart failure with reduced and non-reduced ejection fraction.
items.abstract: Initiation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) after stabilization of an acute heart failure (AHF) episode is well-tolerated and improves outcomes. In this study, we evaluated GDMT eligibility across the spectrum of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in a contemporary AHF population. Data from VancOuver CoastAL Acute Heart Failure Audit (VOCAL-AHF) of patients discharged with AHF were retrospectively analyzed. Eligibility for GDMT was determined based on major society guidelines. Heart failure phenotypes were defined as HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), HFmrEF (41-49%), and HFpEF (≥50%). Among 1587 patients in VOCAL-AHF, there were 782 (49.3%) HFrEF, 132 (8.3%) HFmrEF, and 673 (42.4%) HFpEF. Mean age was 73±15 years and 58% were men. In HFrEF, eligibility for angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI) was 64.4%, β-blockers 89.6%, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) 73.8%, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) 82.2%. Overall, 64.5% were eligible for quadruple therapy. In HFmrEF, 60.6% were eligible for steroidal MRA, 66.7% for SGLT2i, and 56.8% for ARNI with 56% candidate for initiation of all three agents. Eligibility for finerenone was 62.1% based on clinical criteria and 34.1% based on strict trial criteria. Corresponding values in HFpEF were 67.4%, and 37.1%. Overall, 66.6% of patients with non-reduced EF were eligible for dual-therapy with finerenone and SGLT2i. Most patients with AHF, across LVEF categories, are eligible for in-hospital GDMT initiation, with a substantial proportion of those with non-reduced EF also meeting criteria for contemporary disease-modifying therapies, highlighting an important and previously underrecognized therapeutic opportunity in this population.

items.title: ClinicalAge, a framework for modelling ageing trajectories from longitudinal electronic health records in the UK: a model development and validation study.
items.abstract: Ageing is a key determinant of morbidity and mortality. In this study, we aimed to develop and assess a new ageing biomarker, ClinicalAge, derived from routinely collected longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data. In this model development and validation study, we used UK Biobank data for model development and UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum data for model validation. The UK Biobank is a longitudinal population-based cohort of approximately 500 000 individuals aged 40-69 years at recruitment (March 16, 2006, to Oct 1, 2010), with linked EHR from the November 2022 UK Biobank data release. CPRD Aurum is a primary care EHR database containing anonymised longitudinal data from over 30 million patients across the UK, including diagnoses, medication, procedures, and laboratory results. A transformer-based deep learning model was trained from longitudinal EHR data to generate ClinicalAge using the validated biomarker PhenoAge as reference. We used a UK Biobank cohort for model development and internal validation, and three CPRD Aurum cohorts for external validation, longitudinal trajectory analysis, and comparison with the electronic frailty index. ClinicalAge was evaluated for associations with 17 functional measures, ten biological ageing biomarkers, 31 ageing-related diseases (11 cancer diagnoses and 20 non-cancer diseases), and all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular mortality. We further examined longitudinal ClinicalAge trajectories and investigated clinical and disease-specific factors associated with accelerated ageing. The UK Biobank cohort included 320 891 participants (median chronological age 58·0 years [IQR 51·0-63·0]; median PhenoAge 56·0 years [48·6-62·0]; 173 067 [53·9%] were female; and 147 824 [46·1%] were male) and the CPRD cohort included 4 728 376 individuals (51·0 years [44·0-60·0]; 2 293 243 [48·5%] were female and 2 435 133 [51·5%] were male). ClinicalAge had an R 2 score of 0·819 with PhenoAge and showed a significant association with the 17 functional measures and ten biological ageing biomarkers. It was also significantly associated with the incidence of all 20 non-cancer diseases in both datasets, as well as nine (82%) of 11 cancers in UK Biobank (seven positive associations and two negative) and ten (91%) of 11 cancers (eight positive associations and two negative) in CPRD. Moreover, ClinicalAge was significantly associated with all-cause mortality (UK Biobank adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1·23 [95% CI 1·21-1·24]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·36 [1·36-1·36]), cancer mortality (UK Biobank adjusted HR 1·12 [1·10-1·14]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·17 [1·16-1·17]), and cardiovascular mortality (UK Biobank adjusted HR 1·33 [1·29-1·36]; CPRD adjusted HR 1·36 [1·35-1·36]), after adjustment for clinical covariates and lifestyle factors. Midlife was identified as a key window for divergence, with early acceleration in individuals developing diabetes, hypertension, depression, or lifestyle disorders. ClinicalAge is a non-invasive biomarker that leverages routinely collected EHR data to quantify ageing across the life course. It shows strong associations with ageing-related biomarkers, functional decline, disease risk, and mortality. Its interpretability and anticipatory signal offer a practical tool for the early identification of individuals at risk of accelerated ageing, enabling targeted preventive strategies such as lifestyle modification, cardiometabolic control, and mental health support. None.

items.title: Gut microbiota-targeted interventions with probiotics, prebiotics or synbiotics in acute and stable coronary artery disease: A scoping review of human evidence.
items.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been implicated in atherogenesis and the systemic inflammatory pathways underlying acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Synbiotics, which combine prebiotic substrates with live probiotic microorganisms, may provide complementary microbiota-modulating effects. However, their role in coronary artery disease (CAD), particularly after ACS, remains unclear. We conducted a scoping review of PubMed, Ovid, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, Embase and Web of Science from inception to September 2026. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed human studies evaluating probiotic, prebiotic or synbiotic supplementation in acute and stable CAD. Preclinical studies and studies limited to anthropometric, lipid or glucose outcomes were excluded. Ongoing registered clinical trials were also screened. Among 2085 records, six studies met the inclusion criteria: three randomized controlled trials, one non-randomized controlled intervention study, one before-after study and one cross-sectional study. Importantly, no study enrolled patients with ACS. Randomized trials reported improvements in inflammatory biomarkers, angina symptoms and endothelial function. Two synbiotic interventions reduced circulating lipopolysaccharide and inflammatory cytokines, with improved nitric oxide bioavailability in one study. No study assessed major adverse cardiovascular events, recurrent ACS or mortality as pre-specified endpoints. Screening of ongoing trials identified only one registered randomized trial specifically investigating synbiotic supplementation after ACS. This review identified a specific evidence gap: despite mechanistic and biomarker evidence supporting microbiota modulation in stable CAD, its role after ACS remains largely unstudied. Our group is conducting SYMBIO-ACS, a randomized pilot trial of synbiotic supplementation after ACS (NCT07411287), to generate initial mechanistic and clinical evidence.

Pilomatrix-like High-Grade Endometrioid Carcinoma in the Female Genital Tract: A Single-Institution Clinicopathologic Analysis of 15 Cases.
items.abstract: Pilomatrix-like high-grade endometrioid carcinoma (PiMHEC) is a rare endometrial neoplasm with incompletely defined diagnostic criteria and molecular pathogenesis. Clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and genomic features were analyzed in 15 PiMHEC cases: 14 uterine PiMHECs and 1 case with PiMHEC confined to an ovarian metastasis from a uterine low-grade endometrioid carcinoma (LGEC). All PiMHECs contained a dominant high-grade basaloid component (HGBC) with nested architecture and geographic necrosis; shadow cells were present in 12 of 15 cases. Concurrent LGEC (n=10) and atypical hyperplasia (n=6) were identified. The HGBC lacked ER, PR, and PAX8 expression, showed aberrant nuclear β-catenin accumulation, and expressed CD10 and CDX2 in all cases. CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations were detected in 13 cases; the remaining 2 CTNNB1-wildtype tumors harbored truncating APC mutations. PI3K/AKT pathway gene alterations were present in all cases and ARID1A alterations in 14 of 15 cases. Shared somatic mutations were identified in 4 paired HGBC and LGEC cases. Among 13 evaluable surgical specimens, metastases occurred with extensive lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in 60% (3/5), focal LVSI in 80% (4/5), and no LVSI in 33% (1/3). Outcomes differed by molecular subtype: 6/8 no specific molecular profile (NSMP) patients died within one year, whereas all seven deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) patients were alive at last follow-up. Two dMMR patients received immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-containing regimens, with one durable response and one immune-mediated colitis-related discontinuation. These findings support PiMHEC derivation from an LGEC; the entity is characterized by Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation, with APC inactivation representing a potential novel alternative driver in CTNNB1-wildtype tumors. The differing outcomes between NSMP and dMMR tumors require cautious interpretation given the small cohort and ICI exposure in a subset of dMMR patients; nevertheless, ICI therapy warrants further evaluation in dMMR PiMHEC.

items.title: Ligand/receptor-based chimeric antigen receptors: a promising alternative to conventional scFv designs in cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Engineering immune cells, particularly T lymphocytes, with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) has become one of the most successful modalities of cancer immunotherapy, as evidenced by the approval and clinical use of multiple CAR-T cell products. Current CAR platforms predominantly rely on monoclonal antibody-derived single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) for target recognition. While scFv-based CARs have achieved remarkable clinical successes, they also exhibit notable limitations, including the potential to elicit anti-CAR immune responses, tonic signaling that contributes to CAR-T cell exhaustion, tumor escape via antigen loss or downregulation, and on-target, off-tumor toxicities. In response, researchers have explored alternative binding moieties for CAR architectures. Natural ligands and receptors represent one such class of alternatives. These approaches may offer advantages over conventional scFv-based CARs, such as potentially lower immunogenicity with fully human-derived domains, the ability to engage multiple targets or ligands, access to antigens that are challenging for scFvs, and the use of protein-protein interfaces shaped by evolution within human physiology. However, these benefits are not absolute. CAR junctions, non-native orientations, expression levels, modifications, and the cellular context can still generate immunogenic epitopes or dysfunctional products. Additionally, natural ligand/receptor pairs may transmit unwanted agonistic or regulatory signals that require careful engineering to mitigate. This review discusses recent advances in ligand/receptor-based CARs from a translational perspective. It also provides a critical overview of their inherent limitations, alongside potential solutions to support the rational design of next-generation constructs.

items.title: LGALS9 interacts with CD44 on CD8 + T cells to impair activation and mediate immune evasion in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
items.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) shows distinct distribution, and immunotherapy efficacy is limited by T cell dysfunction. Galectin-9 (LGALS9) has immunomodulatory roles, but its mechanism in NPC immune evasion remains unclear. Using scRNA-seq data from GEO, we analyzed the NPC immune microenvironment and identified key ligand-receptor pairs. LGALS9 and CD44 expression were validated by immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, and western blot. CD8 + T cell function was assessed by flow cytometry, ELISA, and LDH release assay. The association between LGALS9 and CD44 was examined by coimmunoprecipitation, and a mouse model evaluated LGALS9 knockdown and CD44 antibody treatment. LGALS9 was upregulated in NPC and negatively correlated with CD8 + T cell infiltration. The LGALS9-CD44 association suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation, increasing PD1 + cells, decreasing GZMB + cells and TNF-α/IFN-γ levels. Blocking this interaction restored T cell activity. LGALS9 knockdown inhibited tumor growth, and CD44 antibody blockade further potentiated the antitumor immune effect induced by LGALS9 knockdown. LGALS9 promotes NPC immune evasion through its association with CD44 on CD8 + T cells in vitro, and in vivo CD44 blockade is consistent with this mechanism, providing a rationale for targeting the LGALS9-CD44 axis.

items.title: Microneedle-based delivery strategies for cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Microneedle (MN) technologies are currently investigated as versatile delivery platforms for cancer immunotherapy. They offer minimally invasive and localized delivery, and may enable sustained release while overcoming several limitations of conventional systemic administration. In this review, we discuss the relation between MN design and the delivery of different cancer immunotherapies, with a particular focus on matching MN technologies to different therapeutic strategies. We first describe the main MN approaches, including dissolving, direct-injection, melting, and diffusion-based systems, and their applications in cancer immunotherapy. We then categorize these applications into four major strategies: cancer vaccination including both prophylactic and therapeutic vaccines, induction of immunogenic cell death using chemotherapeutics and photosensitizers, systemic immunotherapy through transdermal delivery, and local immunomodulation through intratumoral delivery of immunotherapeutic agents. Finally, we discuss current challenges and perspectives for translating MN-based cancer immunotherapies toward clinical application, including formulation flexibility, manufacturing scalability, dose control, and regulatory considerations.

CAB-LA PrEP Prescriptions and Abandonment in the United States, January 2022-June 2025.
items.abstract: Injectable long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA) for HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2021. A national assessment of CAB-LA PrEP abandonment, defined as not filling any prescription, could inform national PrEP implementation efforts. We conducted a national observational cohort study using IQVIA Longitudinal Prescription data to characterize persons prescribed CAB-LA or daily oral PrEP (DO-PrEP) in the United States during January 2022-June 2025. We compared 6-month abandonment risk among individuals with an index CAB-LA or DO-PrEP prescription during 2022-2024. Associations were estimated using multivariable modified Poisson regression models and reported as adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The number of individuals prescribed CAB-LA PrEP increased from 4,645 in 2022 to 23,378 in 2024 and 25,018 during January-June 2025. The proportion of individuals receiving CAB-LA increased from 0.1% in quarter 1 of 2022 to 5.4% in quarter 2 of 2025. While women had a higher 6-month PrEP abandonment risk than men, regardless of PrEP regimen, they were less likely to abandon CAB-LA (11.9%) than DO-PrEP (18.1%, aRR=0.68, 95% CI: 0.62-0.74). The opposite was observed for men, with men more likely to abandon CAB-LA PrEP (10.2%) than DO-PrEP (8.1%, aRR=1.25, 95% CI: 1.20-1.31). CAB-LA PrEP prescribing increased steadily during the first 3.5 years after approval; abandonment risk differed by PrEP regimen and sex. Addressing barriers to injectable and daily oral PrEP uptake, and strengthening sex-specific PrEP implementation strategies, may further reduce abandonment risk.

items.title: Association of ATP7A and ATP7B Variants with Treatment Response in Copper-Associated Hepatitis in the Labrador retriever.
items.abstract: Copper-associated hepatitis in Labrador retrievers is typically treated with copper-restricted diets and D-penicillamine (D-pen). Individual responses in necessary treatment duration and reaccumulation of copper after treatment vary. This exploratory study investigated whether genotype for ATP7B:c.4358G>A and ATP7A:c.980C>T, which are correlated with hepatic copper levels, is associated with this variation in treatment response. Three previously published studies were reanalysed. One retrospective study of hepatic copper decline during D-pen treatment (n=43), and two prospective studies of hepatic copper levels during copper-restricted feeding: one in Labrador retrievers with subclinical copper accumulation (n=28) and one in Labrador retrievers after successful D-pen treatment (n=16). Models of original studies were updated with genotype, and, for the D-pen study, also with diet. Hepatic copper decline during D-pen treatment was analysed with a mixed model and with linear regression of the average monthly decline until the first follow-up biopsy. Copper normalisation on a copper-restricted diet was analysed with logistic regression. In D-pen-treated dogs, ATP7B:c.4358G>A was associated with slower hepatic copper decline (76mg/kg dwl/month per variant allele; 95% CI: 29.4 to 122.7; p T showed a non-significant trend towards faster hepatic copper decline (-72.7mg/kg dwl/month; 95% CI: -146.2 to 0.9; p = 0.06). In dogs with subclinical hepatic copper accumulation, ATP7B:c.4358G>A was associated with higher odds of failing to normalise hepatic copper on a copper-restricted diet (odds ratio 13.0 per variant allele; 95% CI 2.2 to 255.4; p A was associated with slower hepatic copper decline in D-pen-treated Labrador retrievers. Additionally, ATP7B:c.4358G>A was associated with a lower likelihood of hepatic copper normalisation during copper-restricted feeding. The association between ATP7A:c.980C>T and faster hepatic copper decline was weaker and needs confirmation. These exploratory findings warrant prospective studies to determine whether genetic testing can help guide treatment of Labrador retrievers with copper-associated hepatitis.

items.title: Hepatitis E Virus in immunosuppressed patients in the era of global mobility.
items.abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) has emerged as a major, yet under-recognized, public health challenge worldwide, particularly in the context of increasing global mobility and expanding populations of immunosuppressed individuals. Zoonotic HEV, now the leading cause of acute viral hepatitis in Europe, is hindered by markedly heterogeneous surveillance systems, diagnostic strategies, and preventive policies, which limit cross-country comparability obscuring the true disease burden. Underdiagnosis is compounded by the existence of extrahepatic manifestations that escape conventional hepatotropic case definitions. At the same time, chronic HEV infection has gained clinical relevance among immunocompromised hosts, including solid organ transplant recipients, patients with hematologic malignancies, and those receiving biologic or other immunomodulatory therapies. However, the mechanisms driving viral persistence, progression to chronicity, and optimal antiviral management remain incompletely defined. This review synthesizes current epidemiological, clinical, and virological knowledge on HEV in Europe, with a focus on the implications of global migration, and the growing population at risk due to immunosuppression. It highlights key gaps and priority areas, particularly the management of infection in immunocompromised hosts and the development and implementation of targeted vaccination strategies for high-risk groups. In conclusion, integrated cross-disciplinary action is needed in response to this emerging threat.

items.title: Hepatitis A vaccination coverage among adolescents aged 13-17 years, United States, 2024.
items.abstract: Hepatitis A is a vaccine-preventable viral disease that causes inflammation of the liver. The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) incrementally expanded childhood hepatitis A (HepA) vaccine recommendations from 1996 to 2006, the year when universal childhood vaccination was recommended. In 2020, ACIP recommended catch-up vaccination for children and adolescents aged 2-18 years who had not previously received HepA vaccine at any age. We analyzed data from the National Immunization Survey-Teen (NIS-Teen) to assess HepA series initiation (1-dose) and completion (≥ 2-doses) among adolescents aged 13-17 years in the United States during 2024, identify factors associated with HepA series completion among adolescents, and evaluate changes in HepA vaccination coverage among adolescents since the 2020 ACIP catch-up vaccination recommendation by comparing NIS-Teen data from 2019 to data from 2024. In 2024, national HepA vaccination coverage among adolescents was 91.8% (95% CI, 91.1%, 92.5%) for series initiation and 87.1% (95% CI, 86.1%, 88.0%) for series completion. Jurisdiction-level ≥ 2-dose coverage ranged from a low of 71.2% in Mississippi (95% CI, 63.9%, 77.6%) to a high of 97.5% in Georgia (95% CI, 93.4%, 99.1%). Adolescents who received an 11-12-year-old well child exam or checkup, saw a physician at least once during the past 12 months, had a mother aged ≥45 years, or had a mother with at least some college education were significantly more likely to have received ≥2 doses of HepA vaccine. Compared to 2019, significant increases occurred among U.S. adolescents in both HepA series initiation (7.4 percentage point [pct pt] increase in 1-dose coverage) and series completion (9.9 pct pt increase in ≥2-dose coverage) in 2024 (p < .05). HepA vaccination coverage improved among U.S. adolescents following the introduction of the 2020 ACIP catch-up vaccination recommendation.

items.title: Total-Body 18 F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18 F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18 F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10 -5 ), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18 F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18 F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

items.title: Comparable Daughter Radionuclide Redistribution with Superior Tumor Absorbed Dose of the SSTR2 Antagonist [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 Versus [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE.
items.abstract: It has been hypothesized that effective cellular internalization is required for the retention of 225 Ac daughter radionuclides. Both the complex decay chain of 225 Ac and the recoil-mediated release of daughters, particularly 213 Bi (half-life, 46 min), raise concerns about redistribution that may reduce tumor absorbed dose (TAD) and increase off-target radiation exposure. Because somatostatin receptor subtype 2 antagonists, such as satoreotide tetraxetan (SSO110, also known as DOTA-JR11), are not internalized, it has been proposed that the daughter radionuclides are less effectively retained compared with internalizing agonists, such as DOTATATE. In this study, we performed a direct and quantitative comparison of daughter radionuclide redistribution after administration of [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 and [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Methods: Biodistribution and 213 Bi redistribution were evaluated in BALB/c nude mice bearing NCI-H69 small cell lung cancer xenografts. Repeated γ-counting combined with biexponential modeling was used to quantify 225 Ac and 213 Bi activity in tumors, blood, bone marrow, kidneys, the liver, and the intestines up to 96 h postinjection. TAD was calculated with and without accounting for experimentally derived 213 Bi redistribution. Real-time in vitro binding assays were conducted to characterize cellular retention of [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110. Results: [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 demonstrated higher tumor uptake and prolonged retention compared with [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution of 213 Bi from tumors was minimal and comparable between the agonist and antagonist and reduced the TAD by 4.5% for [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 and 3.9% for [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. After accounting for this redistribution, [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 delivered a 2.8-fold higher TAD and a 1.8-fold higher tumor-to-kidney absorbed dose (AD) ratio compared with [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Moreover, 213 Bi redistribution had no relevant impact on AD estimates in evaluated healthy organs, including the kidneys, the intestines, blood, and bone marrow. Real-time binding studies demonstrated a sustained cell-associated β - -signal after incubation with [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110. Conclusion: Despite negligible internalization, [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 did not show increased macroscopic 213 Bi redistribution compared with the internalizing agonist [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution was limited for both radiopeptides and had only a minor effect on AD estimates for tumors and the evaluated healthy tissues. [ 225 Ac]Ac-SSO110 achieved a higher TAD and more favorable tumor-to-kidney ratio compared with [ 225 Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Overall, these findings support further evaluation of antagonist-based 225 Ac radiopharmaceutical therapy.

items.title: A miR-221-3p-CDKN1B-CDK4/β-catenin axis couples tumor progression with response to CDK4/6 inhibition in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Dysregulation of cell cycle control contributes to the progression and therapeutic resistance of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), yet the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that the cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor Dalpiciclib suppresses ICC progression, although its efficacy varies across patient-derived models. Mechanistically, Dalpiciclib inhibits CDK4-mediated phosphorylation of β-catenin at Ser675, thereby attenuating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastatic phenotypes. We further identify miR-221-3p as a key post-transcriptional regulator of CDK4 signaling that modulates both ICC progression and sensitivity to dalpiciclib. Elevated miR-221-3p promotes CDKN1B downregulation, thereby relieving its inhibitory effect on CDK4, enhancing β-catenin phosphorylation, and facilitating metastatic progression. Notably, circulating miR-221-3p levels closely mirrored intratumoral miR-221-3p expression and were associated with Dalpiciclib sensitivity in corresponding patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, suggesting its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for assessing treatment response. Collectively, these findings identify a miR-221-3p/CDKN1B/CDK4/β-catenin axis that links cell cycle regulation ICC progression and CDK4 inhibitor response, providing a mechanistic rationale for preclinical evaluation of Dalpiciclib treatment in ICC.

items.title: Attrition Factors in Patients with Metastatic Melanoma Screened for Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocyte Therapy.
items.abstract: Following recent regulatory approval, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy has entered the treatment landscape for advanced melanoma, but its delivery requires coordinated multidisciplinary care, including surgical tumor procurement (TIL harvest), cellular manufacturing, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and high-dose interleukin-2. Real-world attrition across this pathway remains incompletely characterized. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 59 patients with anti-programmed death 1-refractory metastatic melanoma referred for TIL therapy. Patients were categorized into 4 cohorts: eligible, underwent TIL harvest, and received TIL infusion (cohort A); eligible, underwent TIL harvest, but did not receive infusion (cohort B); eligible, but did not undergo TIL harvest (cohort C); and ineligible (cohort D). We evaluated attrition factors, exploratory predictors of pathway completion, and clinical outcomes among treated patients. Of 59 referred patients, 25 (42.4%) were in cohort A, 9 (15.3%) in cohort B, 17 (28.8%) in cohort C, and 8 (13.6%) in cohort D. The most common reasons for attrition were rapid disease progression and decline in performance status, occurring both before procurement and after TIL harvest but before infusion. The out-of-specification product rate was 14.7% (5/34 patients who underwent procurement); 2 of these 5 patients did not receive infusion. No baseline factor, including M substage, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), number of prior treatment lines, treatment immediately before evaluation, or liver or brain metastases, was significantly associated with undergoing TIL harvest. Elevated LDH at TIL evaluation was significantly associated with higher odds of not receiving infusion after procurement (odds ratio, 12.0; 95% CI, 1.22-117.8; P=0.02). Among treated patients, median time from evaluation to TIL harvest was 41 days and from TIL harvest to infusion was 50 days. Among 22 response-evaluable patients, the overall response rate was 40.9%, disease control rate was 59.1%, median progression-free survival was 2.27 months, and median overall survival was 6.11 months. Real-world attrition during TIL therapy was substantial and was driven predominantly by clinical deterioration rather than manufacturing failure alone. These findings support earlier referral, streamlined care pathways, and refined patient selection to improve successful TIL delivery in advanced melanoma.

items.title: Joint-embedding self-supervised representation learning for robust cone-beam CT segmentation.
items.abstract: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) segmentation is challenged by reconstruction artifacts and limited reliable annotations. We investigate joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-style self-supervised learning for volumetric CBCT segmentation using CBCT-LGR, which extends our preliminary slice-wise conference study through fully three-dimensional local-global encoding, learnable semantic tokens, and a combined objective comprising local-global alignment, semantic alignment, and predictive consistency. We compare CBCT-LGR with supervised baselines (nnU-Net and STU-Net), generic self-supervised methods (BYOL-Med3D and Models Genesis), and foundation models (SAM, MedSAM, and Anatomix) using harmonized patient-level splits, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics while retaining each method's stated supervision setting. For representation-learning methods, frozen encoders are evaluated using supervised decoders trained with the same 10-subject labeled-data budget per dataset. Across three datasets, CBCT-LGR outperforms the generic self-supervised baselines on dataset-average overlap and boundary metrics. On CBCTLiTS, supervised and fine-tuned foundation-model approaches achieve higher absolute DSC under clean reconstruction conditions. Across five controlled reconstruction-quality levels, however, CBCT-LGR exhibits the smallest maximum relative DSC decline among all nine methods, with declines of 1.5% for liver and 14.5% for tumor, and achieves the highest numerical tumor DSC at the two most degraded levels. Results on Dataset 1 quantify agreement with imperfect reference annotations and do not establish true anatomical accuracy or a definitive method ranking. These findings define the capabilities and limitations of JEPA-style pretraining for volumetric CBCT segmentation.
